findings.title: Customer self-reports unfamiliarity with reporting dashboard (not a product defect)
findings.description: Marcus says he personally never learned the reporting features well enough to pull board-ready engagement numbers, but explicitly frames this as his own fault ('me-not-clicking-around problem, not a you problem') rather than a product issue. Tomás resolves it by offering a free 30-minute walkthrough session in August, a services/enablement fix, not a product change. No defect or missing capability in the reporting feature itself is described.
findings.quote: I'd say I personally wish I understood the platform's reporting better, but that's a me-not-clicking-around problem, not a you problem.
findings.severity_reason: Explicitly disclaimed as user error with no product impact described; resolved via a training session rather than any product change.
findings.match_note: Not a product complaint at all — customer explicitly rules out a product cause; no catalogue issue applies.

findings.title: Customer requests phased/pilot billing structure for fall expansion (contract/business ask)
findings.description: Marcus asks whether the planned fall expansion to teacher-leaders could be phased so he isn't asking his school board to approve a large line item all at once. Tomás proposes starting with a small pilot group and expanding once proven, which they agree to revisit as a business conversation in the fall. This concerns program rollout/contract structuring and board budgeting optics, not a BetterBark product capability, defect, or missing feature.
findings.quote: is there a way to phase it so I'm not asking my board for a huge number all at once? They spook easily at big line items.
findings.severity_reason: Purely a commercial/rollout planning question with no product functionality involved.
findings.match_note: No catalogue issue applies — this is a pricing/contract-phasing discussion, not a product bug or feature request.
